The slide presents a technical diagram of a neural network architecture for action prediction. The top half features a horizontal flowchart starting from the left with a vertical sequence of 3D human mesh models (labeled S0 to ST) enclosed in a dashed gray box. A series of arrows connects three green 't-patch Module' blocks in a sequence, with mathematical labels above the arrows indicating subsampled sets and feature functions. To the right of the modules, a pooling operation leads to a stack of brown rectangles representing a T x C feature map, which then feeds into a light blue 'FC' (Fully Connected) block. The final output on the far right is labeled 'Action prediction (per frame)'. Below this main diagram, there are two lines of explanatory text: the first line, in green, describes a 'Subsample' process using farthest point sampling (FPS) with a corresponding mathematical equation; the second line, in black, describes the hierarchical computation of a 'high-dimensional representation' denoted as fl. The overall layout is clean with a white background and moderate text density focused on explaining the model's components.

The slide presents a detailed architecture diagram for a neural network model. On the far left, a vertical dashed box contains a sequence of 3D human mesh models labeled from S^0 to S^T, representing temporal frames. The top half of the slide shows a sequential pipeline where data flows through three green 't-patch Module' blocks. The output of the final module passes through a pooling layer and a set of feature maps to a blue 'FC' (Fully Connected) block, which generates an 'Action prediction (per frame)'. Below this main pipeline, a large light-green box provides a detailed 'zoom-in' view of a single 't-patch Module'. Inside this detailed view, a pink 't-patch Extractor' processes inputs to identify various 3D temporal patches shown in a dashed box. These patches are then fed into multiple orange 't-patch Net' blocks with shared weights, producing feature maps of size T x C. The diagram uses a variety of colors (green, pink, orange, blue) to distinguish different components and includes mathematical notation for data dimensions and feature labels throughout.
